# Disclos

> Disclos helps SaaS companies meet the EU AI Act, Regulation (EU) 2024/1689, three ways: free self-serve tools, live-site monitoring from €49 a month, and a one-time human audit at €997 that includes a year of monitoring. The audit delivers a PDF report, a Loom walkthrough, copy-paste Article 50 disclosure code, and compliance templates in 5 business days, refund-guaranteed.

## Quick facts

- Offering: three tiers. (1) Free self-serve tools. (2) Monitoring subscription from €49 per month. (3) One-time €997 human audit that includes 12 months of monitoring.
- Audit: 5-day EU AI Act compliance audit for SaaS, €997 one-time, refund-guaranteed, includes 12 months of monitoring.
- Monitoring (from €49/month): a weekly check that your live site still shows the required Article 50 disclosure, a compliance score out of 100, an AI feature registry that auto-classifies each feature against the Act and alerts you when a feature changes, and an obligations tracker. Dashboard at https://www.disclos.eu/login
- Free tools: a one-line SDK that shows the Article 50 AI notice in 24 EU languages, a penalty calculator, an Annex III high-risk triage, an Article 50 disclosure generator, a scope check, and two MCP servers for Claude and Cursor (mcp.disclos.eu and article50.disclos.eu).
- Deliverables (audit): PDF audit report, Loom video walkthrough, copy-paste Article 50 disclosure code, internal compliance templates.
- Operator: Disclos, an independent research practice. Founder Gatis Ozols, registered in Latvia, EU. Not a law firm; reports are not legal advice.
- Enforcement deadlines: Article 50 transparency 2 August 2026; Annex III high-risk 2 December 2027; Annex I product safety 2 August 2028 (dates per the AI Omnibus).
- Regulation reference: Regulation (EU) 2024/1689, known as the EU AI Act
- Website: https://www.disclos.eu
- Contact: gatis@disclos.eu

## Who needs an EU AI Act audit

Any SaaS company that:
- Places an AI system on the EU market, or
- Provides AI output used by people in the EU, even if the company is established outside the EU

This covers most modern SaaS using machine learning, large language models, recommendation systems, or generative AI features. Article 2 of Regulation (EU) 2024/1689 defines the territorial scope.

## EU AI Act timeline (post AI Omnibus, May 2026)

- 1 August 2024: Regulation entered into force
- 2 February 2025: Prohibited AI systems banned under Article 5
- 2 August 2025: General-purpose AI model obligations apply (Chapter V)
- 2 August 2026: Article 50 transparency obligations apply (chatbots, AI-generated content, deepfakes, emotion recognition / biometric categorisation disclosures). Penalty regime activates.
- 2 December 2027: Annex III high-risk obligations apply (biometric ID, critical infrastructure, education, employment, essential services, law enforcement, migration, justice). Pushed from 2 August 2026 by the AI Omnibus.
- 2 August 2028: Annex I embedded high-risk systems apply (lifts, toys, machinery, medical devices under Union harmonisation legislation). Pushed from 2 August 2027 by the AI Omnibus.

## AI Omnibus amendments (May 2026)

The European Commission proposed the AI Omnibus on 19 November 2025. A political agreement was reached on 7 May 2026. Key changes:

- High-risk Annex III obligations pushed from 2 August 2026 to 2 December 2027
- Annex I embedded systems pushed from 2 August 2027 to 2 August 2028
- Article 50 transparency obligations unchanged at 2 August 2026
- Penalty regime activation unchanged
- Prohibitions under Article 5 unchanged (effective since 2 February 2025)
- General-purpose AI model obligations unchanged (effective since 2 August 2025)

The Omnibus extension applies to compliance obligations only. The substantive Annex III classification rules are unchanged. SaaS founders building high-risk systems still need the same compliance work, just with more time.

## Risk categories under the EU AI Act

- Unacceptable risk: banned outright under Article 5. Examples include social scoring by public authorities, untargeted facial image scraping, and manipulative AI that exploits vulnerabilities.
- High risk: regulated under Annex III. Requires a conformity assessment, risk management system, technical documentation, human oversight, accuracy, robustness, and cybersecurity controls.
- Limited risk: transparency obligations under Article 50. Examples include chatbots, AI-generated content, deepfakes, and emotion recognition.
- Minimal risk: no obligations beyond voluntary codes of conduct.

## Annex III high-risk areas

1. Biometric identification and categorisation
2. Critical infrastructure (water, gas, electricity, traffic management)
3. Education and vocational training (admissions, grading, monitoring)
4. Employment, worker management, access to self-employment (CV screening, performance evaluation, task allocation, termination)
5. Access to and enjoyment of essential public and private services (creditworthiness scoring, public benefits, emergency services dispatch, health and life insurance)
6. Law enforcement
7. Migration, asylum, border control management
8. Administration of justice and democratic processes

## Article 50 transparency obligations

Article 50 applies to AI systems that interact with humans, generate synthetic content, perform emotion recognition, or perform biometric categorisation. Required actions:

- Disclose to users when they are interacting with an AI system
- Mark AI-generated content as machine-readable (watermark, metadata, or visible label)
- Disclose deepfakes as artificially generated or manipulated
- Inform users when emotion recognition or biometric categorisation is used

Article 50 obligations apply from 2 August 2026. Unchanged by the AI Omnibus.

## Penalty bands (Article 99)

- Prohibited AI violations (Article 5): up to €35,000,000 or 7% of total worldwide annual turnover for the preceding financial year, whichever is higher. Effective since 2 February 2025.
- High-risk and Article 50 violations: up to €15,000,000 or 3% of total worldwide annual turnover. Article 50 penalties enforceable from 2 August 2026. High-risk penalties enforceable from 2 December 2027 (Omnibus extension).
- Supplying incorrect, incomplete, or misleading information to notified bodies or national authorities: up to €7,500,000 or 1% of total worldwide annual turnover.

Penalties are set by each Member State's national authority. SMEs and startups: penalties are applied proportionally, taking turnover into account, under Article 99(6).

## Common questions about the EU AI Act

### Does the EU AI Act apply to a US-based SaaS?
Yes if the SaaS produces output used in the EU, or if EU residents use its AI features. Article 2 of Regulation (EU) 2024/1689 applies the Act to providers placing AI systems on the EU market regardless of where the provider is established.

### Is a chatbot high-risk under the EU AI Act?
A chatbot is rarely high-risk by default. It is usually a limited-risk system under Article 50. The operator must disclose to users that they are interacting with an AI system. A conformity assessment is only required if the chatbot performs a task listed in Annex III (for example screening job applicants or evaluating creditworthiness).

### What is an Article 50 disclosure?
A clear, visible statement that the user is interacting with an AI system, given at the start of the interaction. The Disclos team provides a copy-paste HTML snippet and translated versions covering the 24 EU official languages.

### What is the penalty for an EU AI Act violation?
Up to €15,000,000 or 3% of total worldwide annual turnover for most violations, including high-risk and Article 50 breaches. Article 5 prohibited-AI violations face up to €35,000,000 or 7%. Article 50 penalties are enforceable from 2 August 2026. High-risk Annex III penalties are enforceable from 2 December 2027 under the AI Omnibus. SME-proportionality applies under Article 99(6).

### How long does an EU AI Act compliance audit take?
The Disclos audit takes 5 business days, from intake brief to delivered report. The audit covers scoping, risk classification under Annex III, Article 50 transparency drafting, and a final PDF report with sign-off.

### What does the Disclos audit deliver?
A PDF compliance report mapping each AI feature to its risk category, copy-paste Article 50 disclosure code, internal compliance templates (record-keeping, incident reporting, human oversight policy), and a Loom video walkthrough.

### How much does an EU AI Act audit cost?
€997 for the full 5-day audit. One-time fee, refund-guaranteed if the Disclos team cannot deliver. No subscription, no upsell.

### Is there an open-source EU AI Act checklist?
Disclos publishes a self-audit checklist at https://www.disclos.eu/blog. Compliance tools (penalty calculator, Annex III triage, Article 50 disclosure generator) are available at https://www.disclos.eu/tools.

### When does the EU AI Act start applying to SaaS?
Article 50 transparency obligations (chatbots, AI-generated content, deepfakes, biometric disclosures) apply from 2 August 2026. Penalty regime activates the same date. Annex III high-risk obligations (CV screening, credit scoring, education grading, biometric ID) were pushed by the AI Omnibus to 2 December 2027. Prohibited AI bans (Article 5) already apply since 2 February 2025. GPAI model obligations apply since 2 August 2025.

## Open-source EU AI Act checklist on GitHub

Disclos maintains a free, MIT-licensed open-source checklist for SaaS teams running their own EU AI Act self-audit. The repository contains:

- A 7-step plain-English self-audit checklist
- A Python decision-tree script (classify.py) that takes 5 inputs and returns the risk category for any AI feature
- Article 50 disclosure code templates: chatbot HTML (Article 50(1)), synthetic content markers (Article 50(2)), emotion recognition disclosures (Article 50(3)), deepfake disclosures (Article 50(4))
- French translations of all Article 50 templates
- Machine-readable Annex III categorisation (annex-iii-categories.json)
- Machine-readable Article 99 penalty bands (penalty-bands.json)

Repository: https://github.com/GatisOzols/eu-ai-act-checklist

The repository will always stay free. The 5-day Disclos audit applies the same methodology to a customer's specific product.
